items.title: Section: Why "Faculty" Means Mastery, and the Six Reasons Behind All Six Skilful Understandings

items.zh: 於見等事自在相應；於見等事自在相應，是故名根。當知蘊等略由六因而得建立。謂身體建立、彼因建立、身者建立、彼轉方便建立、即於彼轉勝劣方便建立、即彼受用增上建立。
items.en: Holding mastery over seeing and the rest — holding mastery over seeing and the rest is why they are named faculties. It should be understood that the aggregates and the rest are established, in brief, through six causes: the establishment of the body, of its cause, of the one who inhabits it, of that one's activity, of the relative skillfulness of that activity, and of that one's own dominance in experiencing what is encountered.

items.title: Section: Six Wrong Views, Six Cures

items.zh: 復略顯示六種善巧，當知為遣六種邪執。何等為六？一、依止邪執，二、自性自在等不平等因邪執，三、能持依止我邪執，四、彼死生轉邪執，五、彼淨不淨方便邪執，六、彼愛非愛境界受用主宰邪執。
items.en: The six kinds of skilful understanding are further revealed, in brief, to dispel six kinds of wrong view. What are the six? First, the wrong view of a fixed basis for the self; second, the wrong view of an unequal, sovereign cause such as a creator deity; third, the wrong view of a self sustaining and operating the senses; fourth, the wrong view of birth and death's own beginning and end; fifth, the wrong view of invalid means nonetheless leading to purity; and sixth, the wrong view of a self sovereign over experiencing pleasant and unpleasant objects.

items.zh: 問：觀幾勝利，分別建立簡擇諸法、修習善巧？答：略有十種。謂當遍知薩迦耶見，分析一合之想。於有法現有諦故、住故，便不誹謗。自無疑惑，善答他問。未信令信，已信令增。亦令如來聖教久住。

items.title: Section: Ten Benefits, From No Creator God to the Final Exhaustion of Every Outflow

items.zh: 又當悟入緣起道理，能了釋、梵、世主、自性及士夫等非作者，無實性。又令慧根增長廣大，於善不善如實了知，廣說乃至緣生差別。又於善不善法廣說乃至緣生差別，當善住念。由有法隨法行故，即以住念為依止、為建立，當證善心一境之性。又即以此心一境性為依止、為建立，令聖慧根當得生起。依聖慧根，永斷顛倒，隨證漏盡。由觀如是諸勝利故，分別建立簡擇諸法、修習善巧。
items.en: One should also enter into the principle of dependent origination, thereby understanding that Indra, Brahmā, the lord of the world, a self-existent creator, and any personal agent are not the true maker, having no real substance at all. The wisdom faculty grows broad and expansive, genuinely understanding wholesome and unwholesome causes, extending through the distinctions of dependently arisen phenomena. Amid these same distinctions, one comes to genuinely abide in right mindfulness. Through practising in accordance with the Dharma, and resting on that very mindfulness, one attains a wholesome mind's own one-pointed concentration. Resting on that same concentration, noble wisdom is given rise to. Resting on that noble wisdom, distorted views are permanently severed, and the exhaustion of outflows is in due course realised. It is by observing these very benefits that one distinguishes, establishes, and thoroughly cultivates all things through skilful understanding.

items.title: Section: The Close of a Seven-Fascicle Discussion

items.zh: 已略決擇五識身地、意地，於二地中餘決擇文，更不復現。
items.en: Having now, in brief, rendered the decisive determination of the stage associated with the five sense-consciousness-bodies and the stage of mind, no further decisive text concerning these two stages appears beyond this point.

blocks.text: A short day that closes the long discussion of the six skills (aggregates, elements, sense-fields, dependent origination, possible and impossible, faculties).
Master Cháng Bǎi identifies "the one who inhabits the body" with the defiled mind.
Each skill cures a wrong view: no self holds the body and operates things; all things arise from seeds, and the eighteen elements are their true cause.

(Untranslated, 0620c05: ten benefits of studying these things: understanding the view of a self, breaking the notion of a single whole, not denying what exists, freedom from doubt, answering others well, bringing faith to those without it and increasing it in those with it, and making the Tathāgata's teaching last.)
The seven-fascicle discussion of the skills is complete.
The possible and impossible, and the twenty-two faculties. Together with fascicles 53–56, it gives a complete inventory of what a person is made of, so that nothing is left over to be called a self.

quiz.q: The English has "the one who inhabits it" for 身者. What is the problem?
options: no problem: there is a self residing in the body, explaining who receives results, undenied below
the lecture takes 身者 as the defiled mind; the English implies an inhabitant, the very self being refuted here
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi identifies 身者 with the defiled mind. Then §89 refutes the view of a self holding the support: no self dwells in the body operating phenomena. "The one who inhabits it" therefore sounds like the very view being dispelled; a term for the defiled mind or a note is needed.

quiz.q: What are the first three wrong views dispelled, and their remedies?
options: wrong view of the basis by aggregates; of unequal cause by elements; of a sustaining self, shown not to be by the next
the view of a creator by aggregates; of the basis by elements; of birth and death by faculties, without fixed order
all six are refuted by dependent origination
all six are refuted by faculties
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the support is the body, wrongly taken as self, for which the skill in aggregates is set; all phenomena arise from seeds, the eighteen elements being the true cause, which removes the view of unequal cause. The English "a creator deity" brings out 自在 explicitly.
